title: Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: Evaluation and Follow-up
summary: Concise, guideline-aligned approach to risk-stratified evaluation of thyroid nodules and evidence-based follow-up of differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), integrating ATA/ESMO/NICE guidance and recent data on dynamic risk stratification and thyroglobulin monitoring.
clinicalQuestion: How should clinicians evaluate thyroid nodules and implement risk-adapted follow-up for differentiated thyroid cancer to optimize detection, treatment, and surveillance outcomes?

heroStats.label: Excellent response after DTC therapy
heroStats.value: ≈60–85% with low recurrence risk (<2%) on long-term follow-up [1], [2]

heroStats.label: Tg as relapse detector
heroStats.value: High NPV when undetectable off/on LT4; dynamic use central to follow-up [3]

keyMoments.title: Risk-stratify nodules before biopsy
keyMoments.body: Use ultrasound pattern and size thresholds to determine FNA need; avoid unnecessary biopsies in low-suspicion nodules. **FNA remains the most accurate test** for cytologic diagnosis [1], [9].

keyMoments.title: Integrate cytology with molecular testing selectively
keyMoments.body: For indeterminate cytology (Bethesda III–IV), **molecular testing may refine malignancy risk**, guiding surveillance vs surgery in appropriate settings [1].

keyMoments.title: Use dynamic risk stratification
keyMoments.body: Reassess recurrence risk over time using **Tg/anti-Tg trends and imaging response** to tailor TSH targets and intensity of surveillance [1], [2], [3].

keyMoments.title: TSH suppression individualized
keyMoments.body: Stronger suppression for high risk, **relaxation to low-normal TSH** in excellent responders to reduce adverse effects [1], [2].

keyMoments.title: Lean imaging
keyMoments.body: In low-risk DTC with excellent response, **limit cross-sectional imaging and diagnostic RAI scans**; neck ultrasound and Tg suffice [1], [2], [5], [6].

sections.title: Evaluation of Thyroid Nodules
sections.blurb: Prioritize ultrasound-based risk assessment and selective biopsy to minimize overdiagnosis while detecting clinically relevant cancers.

steps.title: Clinical assessment and labs
steps.body:
- Identify risk factors: prior neck irradiation, family history, rapid growth, compressive or invasion symptoms [9].
- Measure TSH; **low TSH → radionuclide scan** to evaluate for autonomously functioning nodules (generally do not require FNA) [1].

steps.title: Ultrasound risk stratification
steps.body:
- Characterize echogenicity, composition, margins, shape, calcifications, and vascularity; assess cervical lymph nodes [1], [9].
- Apply guideline size thresholds for FNA based on **suspicion pattern** (e.g., high suspicion nodules biopsied at smaller sizes than low suspicion) to reduce unnecessary biopsies [1].

steps.title: FNA cytology (Bethesda system) and next steps
steps.body:
- **FNA is the most precise diagnostic test**, guiding surgery vs surveillance [9].
- Bethesda II: observe; Bethesda V–VI: surgical referral; Bethesda III–IV: consider **molecular testing** and patient preference to guide lobectomy vs surveillance [1].

sections.title: Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: Initial Therapy
sections.blurb: Tailor extent of surgery, use of radioactive iodine (RAI), and TSH suppression to recurrence risk.

steps.title: Surgery
steps.body: - Low-risk intrathyroidal tumors: **lobectomy sufficient** in many cases; total thyroidectomy for higher-risk features (extrathyroidal extension, nodal disease, larger tumors) [1], [2].

steps.title: Radioactive iodine (RAI)
steps.body: - Not routine for low-risk DTC; consider for intermediate/high-risk features (e.g., extensive nodal disease, aggressive histology) to facilitate ablation and surveillance [1], [2].

steps.title: TSH suppression
steps.body: - Initial TSH targets: high-risk 0.01–0.1 mU/L; intermediate-risk 0.1–0.5 mU/L; low-risk 0.5–2 mU/L, balancing cardiovascular/bone risks with benefit [1], [2].

sections.title: Follow-up of DTC Using Dynamic Risk Stratification
sections.blurb: Adapt monitoring intensity based on evolving response categories using thyroglobulin (Tg), anti-Tg antibodies, and imaging.

steps.title: Core tools and intervals
steps.body:
- **Serum Tg and anti-Tg antibodies** on LT4 at 6–12 months, then 6–12-monthly depending on risk/response; consider stimulated Tg selectively [1], [3].
- **Neck ultrasound** at 6–12 months; if negative and excellent response, extend intervals to every 12–24 months or longer [1], [2], [5], [6].

steps.title: Response-to-therapy categories
steps.body:
- Excellent response: undetectable/very low Tg, negative imaging → **TSH 0.5–2 mU/L**, minimal imaging; very low recurrence risk [1], [2], [3].
- Biochemical incomplete: elevated/ rising Tg or anti-Tg, negative imaging → intensify surveillance; consider stimulated Tg, cross-sectional imaging if rising [1], [3].
- Structural incomplete: proven disease → **targeted therapy** (surgery, RAI if iodine-avid, or systemic therapy if RAI-refractory) [1], [2].
- Indeterminate: nonspecific findings/low-level Tg → observe trends; many evolve to excellent response [1].

steps.title: Imaging beyond ultrasound
steps.body: - Reserve CT/MRI/FDG-PET for **rising Tg with negative US**, aggressive histology, or suspected distant/RAI-refractory disease [1], [2].

sections.title: Practical Follow-up by Risk/Response
sections.blurb: Suggested surveillance cadence aligned with major guidelines.

cards.title: Low-risk, excellent response
items: TSH: 0.5–2 mU/L; relax suppression to avoid adverse effects [1], [2]
Tg/anti-Tg: annually; extend to every 12–24 months if stable [1], [3]
Neck US: at 6–12 months, then PRN with Tg rise or exam change [1], [2], [5], [6]
Avoid routine diagnostic RAI scans or cross-sectional imaging [1], [2]

cards.title: Intermediate-risk or indeterminate response
items: Tg/anti-Tg: every 6–12 months; consider stimulated Tg if trending upward [1], [3]
Neck US: every 6–12 months initially, then space out if stable [1], [2]
Cross-sectional imaging only if Tg rises or US suspicious [1], [2]

cards.title: High-risk or biochemical incomplete
items: TSH: 0.01–0.1 mU/L while balancing cardiac/bone risk [1], [2]
Tg/anti-Tg: every 3–6 months until stable [1], [3]
Neck US: every 6–12 months; add CT/MRI if Tg rising [1], [2]
Consider empiric/diagnostic RAI or PET/CT if RAI-refractory suspected [1], [2]

cards.title: Structural incomplete response
items: Restage with US ± CT/MRI ± PET; assess iodine avidity [1], [2]
Local therapy: resection, RAI if avid, or EBRT in select cases [2]
Systemic therapy for progressive RAI-refractory disease (e.g., multikinase inhibitors) per ESMO [2]
Bone and CV risk mitigation during prolonged TSH suppression [1], [2]

sections.title: Surveillance of Benign Nodules
sections.blurb: Conservative monitoring prevents overtreatment while identifying change.

cards.title: Benign cytology (Bethesda II)
items: Repeat US at 12–24 months; lengthen interval if stable [1], [9]
Re-biopsy if **significant growth** or new suspicious features [1]
Manage compressive symptoms with surgery or ablation options per resources [1]

cards.title: Indeterminate nodules under surveillance
items: US at 6–12 months, then yearly if stable [1]
Integrate molecular test result with clinical/US risk to decide on lobectomy vs continued observation [1]
